memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "He blessed them that day and said, 'In your name will Israel pronounce this blessing: "May God make you like Ephraim and Manasseh."' So he put Ephraim ahead of Manasseh." — Gen 48:20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This blessing became a permanent part of Israel's life. To this day, in many Jewish homes, a father lays his hands on his sons' heads on the eve of the Sabbath and says these words: May God make you like Ephraim and Manasseh.

It is worth asking why these two, of all people. They did nothing notable. Scripture records no achievement of theirs, no act of courage, no famous moment. They were half-Egyptian boys who were adopted in and blessed.

Perhaps that is exactly the point. They are the picture of a blessing entirely received, not earned. Nothing about their birth qualified them. Everything came from the old man's hand and God's choosing.

Would you want your children to be like that? Not "may God make you successful" or "may God make you impressive," but may God make you like two young men whose whole standing came from grace.

That is a good prayer for anyone. Our deepest hope for those we love should not be that they achieve much, but that they are securely, gratefully included in the family of God through Christ.

There is no better thing to want for a child.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What do you most want for the young people in your life?
2. Have you ever spoken a blessing over someone out loud?
3. Do you rest in a standing you received, or one you are trying to earn?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, my deepest hope for those I love is that they belong to You. Teach me to speak blessing over them, and let me rest in the standing You have given me in Christ. Amen.
